chalcolithic.writing: Pre-literate; pictographic tokens used for accounting in Mesopotamia
chalcolithic.pottery: Ghassulian fine ware; copper implements first appearing
chalcolithic.architecture: Mudbrick villages; early temples at Eridu (Mesopotamia)
chalcolithic.religion: Animistic religion; fertility cults; early temple culture in Mesopotamia
chalcolithic.politics: Village-based tribal societies; early chiefdoms in Levant
chalcolithic.trade: Obsidian, copper, and shell traded regionally across the Near East

early-bronze.writing: Cuneiform invented (~3200 BCE); Egyptian hieroglyphics develop; earliest literary texts
early-bronze.pottery: Wheel-made pottery widespread; Khirbet Kerak ware in Canaan
early-bronze.architecture: Monumental mudbrick temples (ziggurats); Egyptian pyramid construction begins
early-bronze.religion: Sumerian pantheon (Enlil, Enki, Inanna); Egyptian state religion; pharaoh as god-king
early-bronze.politics: Sumerian city-states (Ur, Uruk, Lagash); Old Kingdom Egypt; Akkadian Empire
early-bronze.trade: Lapis lazuli from Afghanistan; cedar from Lebanon; tin from unknown eastern source

middle-bronze.writing: Cuneiform literature flourishes (Epic of Gilgamesh); Proto-Sinaitic alphabet emerging (~1800 BCE)
middle-bronze.pottery: Wheel-made red-burnished ware; Tell el-Ajjul tradition in Canaan
middle-bronze.architecture: Mudbrick city walls with glacis; triple-gate complexes at Megiddo, Hazor, Gezer
middle-bronze.religion: El as chief deity in Canaan; Baal storm-god worship; temples at Megiddo and Shechem
middle-bronze.politics: City-state system under Egyptian influence; Old Babylonian Empire (Hammurabi); Hyksos
middle-bronze.trade: Tin from Afghanistan via Assyrian merchant colonies (karum) at Kanesh; Egyptian trade with Byblos

late-bronze.writing: Alphabetic writing spreading (Ugaritic, early Phoenician); Amarna Letters in Akkadian
late-bronze.pottery: Mycenaean and Cypriot imports; bichrome ware; Canaanite jars for trade
late-bronze.architecture: Egyptian administrative buildings in Canaan; Canaanite temple style (broad-room); palaces
late-bronze.religion: Baal cycle mythology at Ugarit; Egyptian solar religion under Akhenaten; cult of Asherah
late-bronze.politics: Egyptian New Kingdom controls Canaan; Hittite Empire in north; Mitanni, Assyria competing
late-bronze.trade: Pan-Mediterranean Bronze Age trading network; tin from Europe; copper from Cyprus

iron-age-1.writing: Phoenician alphabet spreading; early Hebrew script emerging; Gezer Calendar
iron-age-1.pottery: Collared-rim store jars associated with highland settlements; Philistine bichrome ware
iron-age-1.architecture: Four-room house as Israelite architectural type; Philistine cities (Ashdod, Ekron)
iron-age-1.religion: Yahweh worship establishing; Ba'al conflict; local shrines (bamot); ark of the covenant
iron-age-1.politics: Bronze Age Collapse fragments empires; Philistine pentapolis; tribal confederacy; early monarchy
iron-age-1.trade: Disrupted international trade; local exchange economies; iron metallurgy spreading

iron-age-2.writing: Hebrew ostraca (Samaria Ostraca, Lachish Letters); royal inscriptions; early biblical texts
iron-age-2.pottery: Red-slip ware; Assyrian palace ware in conquered territories; storage jar traditions
iron-age-2.architecture: Israelite royal architecture at Megiddo, Hazor, Gezer (Solomon's gates); Assyrian palaces
iron-age-2.religion: Reform movements; Deuteronomistic theology; Isaiah, Jeremiah, Amos prophesying
iron-age-2.politics: United Monarchy (David/Solomon); Divided Kingdom (Israel/Judah); Assyrian conquest of Israel (722 BCE)
iron-age-2.trade: Phoenician maritime trade; Arabian incense route active; Assyrian tribute system

babylonian-persian.writing: Aramaic becomes international language; Dead Sea region scribal traditions begin
babylonian-persian.pottery: Persian-period ware; Attic imports; mortaria and storage jars
babylonian-persian.architecture: Persian administrative buildings; Second Temple construction begins; Nehemiah's walls
babylonian-persian.religion: Monotheism crystallizing in exile; Torah edited; synagogue origins; Zoroastrian influence
babylonian-persian.politics: Babylonian exile (586–538 BCE); Cyrus Edict; Persian province of Yehud (Judah)
babylonian-persian.trade: Persian royal road system; Aramaic commercial documents; Elephantine Jewish community
